declarations.missingFact: whether the bed-four panel's concrete has reached the strength required for anchor lifting
declarations.observationSpan: nobody can say how long the bed was without heat, and the hall itself was cold
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The observation states the heat loss duration is unknown and the hall was cold, and that the probe reader cannot currently be used and no cube results are reported; it does not state whether the concrete has in fact reached adequate strength.
declarations.branchA: the companion cube tests (or another confirmed method) show the panel has reached adequate strength for lifting
declarations.decisionIfA: the lift on the cast-in anchors may proceed as staged, since the strength basis for the anchors is confirmed
declarations.branchB: the cube tests have not yet confirmed adequate strength, or show the concrete is under-strength
declarations.decisionIfB: the lift must be held, the crew withdrawn from standing by at the bed, and the panel not lifted until strength is confirmed by an alternative verified means
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: the gantry is already rigged and the crew are standing by to lift immediately, so the strength question must be resolved before the lift proceeds rather than after

clarifications.question: Has the concrete in bed four's panel reached the required strength for anchor lifting, established either by the companion cube test results from the laboratory or by any other confirmed reading, given that the maturity probe currently cannot be read on site?

declarations.missingFact: whether the overnight caustic cleaning circuit actually completed and the tank was drained/rinsed before the cycle-complete lamp was observed lit
declarations.observationSpan: a technician reset that panel this morning while clearing an unrelated alarm, and the operator who set the overnight cycle finished at six and has left site
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The observation states the panel was reset this morning for an unrelated alarm and that the operator who ran the cycle has left site, but it does not state whether the cycle-complete lamp's current display reflects the actual completion of that specific overnight cycle or was affected by the reset; it also does not state whether anyone checked the tank interior or drain line for residual caustic.
declarations.branchA: The caustic circuit fully completed its drain and rinse stages before the panel was reset, and the tank interior is free of residual caustic liquid or significant vapour
declarations.decisionIfA: No additional caustic-specific control is needed before entry beyond what is already in place; entry may proceed as planned once other open items are addressed
declarations.branchB: The caustic circuit's completion cannot be confirmed as having included a full drain/rinse before the panel reset, and residual caustic liquid or vapour could remain in the tank or on internal surfaces
declarations.decisionIfB: Entry must be held until the tank interior and drain line (e.g. via the sample cock) are physically checked for residual caustic and confirmed safe, with appropriate PPE for corrosive exposure available before the fitter enters
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: The fitter is already at the manway with tools, about to enter the tank, so whether residual caustic could be present must be resolved before entry proceeds rather than discovered after the fitter is inside a space with restricted egress.

clarifications.question: Has the cycle-complete status of the overnight caustic circuit (including confirmation that the tank was fully drained and rinsed) been independently verified, given that the panel was reset this morning by a technician clearing an unrelated alarm and the operator who ran the cycle has left site?

declarations.missingFact: Whether the trailer restraint lock has actually engaged the trailer's rear underrun bar
declarations.observationSpan: the lamps that show whether the hook has actually taken hold have been dark since the bay's control box was struck by a reversing vehicle last month
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The observation states only that the indicator lamps are dark; it does not state whether the lock has engaged or failed to engage, or whether any alternative check of engagement was made.
declarations.branchA: The lock has physically engaged the underrun bar (confirmed by an alternative method such as a manual check), and the trailer is restrained
declarations.decisionIfA: The lift truck may proceed to drive into the trailer for this hazard, since the restraint is confirmed effective, subject to resolution of the separate deck condition
declarations.branchB: The lock's engagement is unconfirmed or it has not engaged, and the trailer is not reliably restrained
declarations.decisionIfB: Unloading must be halted until the lock is verified engaged by an alternative method, or supplementary restraint (such as wheel chocks) is applied, before the lift truck enters the trailer
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: Unloading is stated to start straight away and the lift truck is about to drive into the trailer, so the restraint state must be known before that entry occurs to prevent a trailer-separation incident.

declarations.missingFact: Whether the reported soft area in the trailer deck has been located, inspected and found safe, or repaired, since it was reported
declarations.observationSpan: a soft area in the deck about a third of the way down, and the deck is covered end to end with protective board laid over it, so none of it can be seen
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The observation states the soft area was reported by a previous driver and that the deck is now covered by board so it cannot be seen; it does not state that the area was inspected, assessed, or remediated after being reported.
declarations.branchA: The soft area was located, inspected, and confirmed safe to drive over or repaired before the board was laid
declarations.decisionIfA: The lift truck may cross the deck as planned for this hazard, since the structural condition has been confirmed adequate, subject to resolution of the separate trailer-restraint condition
declarations.branchB: The soft area was never inspected or remediated and its current structural condition beneath the board is unknown
declarations.decisionIfB: The lift truck must not drive over the deck until the soft area is located and assessed (for example by lifting the board at the reported location or otherwise testing the deck), because a four-tonne-plus front-axle load could cause the weakened deck to fail
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: The lift truck is about to drive the length of the deck to retrieve drummed lubricant, and the board covering means the soft spot cannot be seen or avoided unless its status is known before entry.

clarifications.question: Has the trailer restraint lock's actual engagement with the underrun bar been confirmed by some means other than the dark indicator lamps (for example, a physical check) before the lift truck drives in?
Has the soft area of the trailer deck been located, inspected, and confirmed safe (or repaired) since it was reported, given the deck is now fully covered by protective board?

declarations.missingFact: Whether the reduced-speed, single-step, empty-fixture verification cycle was performed on the reprogrammed path before automatic production resumed
declarations.observationSpan: he could not say whether the reduced-speed cycle was actually run
declarations.notEstablishedBecause: The team leader's own statement establishes only that he cannot say whether the verification cycle occurred; it does not establish that it was run or that it was skipped.
declarations.branchA: The reduced-speed, single-step, empty-fixture cycle was in fact run and the path proved sound before the part was loaded
declarations.decisionIfA: The required program-verification control for this cell has been satisfied; running the current part in automatic is consistent with the cell's standing restart method and no additional stop is needed on this basis
declarations.branchB: The reduced-speed, single-step, empty-fixture cycle was not run before the part was loaded and automatic was engaged
declarations.decisionIfB: Automatic production must be stopped, the part removed from the fixture, and the reduced-speed empty cycle run and verified sound before any further automatic operation with a loaded part
declarations.whyNecessaryNow: The cell is currently running in automatic with a part in the fixture; the cell has a repeat history of driving the torch into the clamp after program changes, so whether the mandated verification step occurred determines whether the ongoing run should continue or be stopped immediately.

clarifications.question: Was the mandated reduced-speed, single-step, empty-fixture verification cycle actually run on this reprogrammed path before the cell was placed in automatic with a part loaded?
